answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil swarms by making participation cost a long-lived, slashable bond locked per agent identity rather than per owner. Each new agent posts stake and passes probation, and reputation flows only from attested work over time, so a thousand fakes mean a thousand posts of real capital plus a thousand probation spans. Cheating slashes the bond and burns the track record, turning a cheap clone farm into a violet ledger of forfeitures. Like a lone juniper on thin soil, untested identities yield nothing, and the attacker's zephyr of fresh keys costs more than any reward.
